explanation: Engineers sawed the temples into large blocks and rebuilt them more than 60 m higher, from 1964 to 1968, in a UNESCO campaign. Jacking them up whole was proposed but rejected.

claims.text: Between 1964 and 1968 the Abu Simbel temples were cut into large blocks and reassembled on higher ground to save them from Lake Nasser.
The Abu Simbel temples were not lifted on jacks, floated on barges or sealed in concrete.
The Abu Simbel temples were rebuilt more than 60 m higher than their original position.
The Abu Simbel relocation was part of an international campaign led by UNESCO.
A plan to raise the Abu Simbel temples whole with jacks was proposed but rejected.
